profile.name: Librarian
profile.description: Builds a personal library site from your actual shelves. Send photos. It catalogs books, pulls snippets, maps contradictions, and marks the ones you'd hand people.

memory.content: Disagreements between snippets are titled contradictions. That is the interesting connection. talks-to is secondary.
Library and site design work uses the impeccable design skill.
On library book pages, the owner's note is a boxed section titled "{name}'s note" above snippets. When they drop a note for a book, add it to that book's ownerNote field.
Handed books are marked with a small black dot before the title (and before the word handed in nav, filters, and the handed header). The handed page explains: the little black dot marks them.
Library homepage default: "these are the books on my actual shelves. just because i read them doesn't mean i agree with them. different perspectives help me connect dots i otherwise couldn't see."
Contradictions intro default: "whenever i read something i try to understand what the opposite view might be. this is my experiment to connect the contradictions in what i read."

Library connections live at the snippet level, not just book-to-book. A snippet is either text pulled from a book or a photo of an underlined passage. Connections (talks-to, contradictions) attach to snippets. Keep this layer simple.
Library shelves use custom hundreds, not Dewey: 000 tech, 100 mind, 200 spirit, 300 world, 400 money, 600 work, 700 making, 800 writing, 900 lives. Novels sit with writing on 800.
Library site nav is catalog, search, snippets, contradictions, handed.
Each library shelf is one horizontal swipeable/scrollable row, with titles under the covers so they do not overlap.
Library cover images are scaled ~1.5× so titles stay readable: 180px desktop and 165px mobile on shelf rows, 240px on book pages.
Each catalog shelf row lists handed books first, then the rest of that shelf.
Handed is the must-read section: "the books i always hand people to read." Books get handed: true when the owner names them.
Library heading reads "on the shelf - N books" with the live catalog count.
Related snippets and contradictions stack as separate rows, each with its book title under it, not as a comma-separated run. They nest under their parent snippet, indented with a thin left rule.
Library book pages have a quiet buy link in the meta line, pointed at a Google search for author plus title (no Amazon lock-in).
Clicking an author name opens a simple page with that author's shelf of books.
A thin line break sits between each pair of contradiction groups.
Search lists books alphabetically by title so the full catalog is a scrollable A-Z.
Host the library on Cloudflare Pages (static zip, Production Direct Upload to an existing project unless they ask for a new one).

name: Impeccable design
description: >-
  Use whenever designing, restyling, or judging UI — especially the library
  site, any new page, or a “this is hard to read” layout pass.
---
# Impeccable design

Use Anthropic’s frontend-design skill as the quality bar. Do not ship a templated layout.

## Before writing CSS or markup

1. Name the subject, the audience, and the page’s single job.
2. Honor the brief exactly when one already exists. For the library that brief is locked: white paper, `#111` ink, Avenir, lowercase, lots of air, 1px rules, no cards, no shadows, no Inter, no purple gradients.
3. Spend boldness in one place. Cut any extra decoration.
4. Structure is information. Labels, dividers, and lists should make the content easier to parse, not decorate it.

## Library-specific

- Snippets are the unit. Connections (contradictions first, talks-to second) must read as separate snippets, each with its book title.
- The owner’s note is a boxed 1px `#111` section titled `{name}'s note`.
- Copy stays in the owner’s voice: lowercase, short, no help-desk tone.

## After a visual change

Look at the real page (screenshot). If a related block is still a comma run, a truncated soup, or missing book context, fix it before calling it done.

skills.content:
---
name: Personal library
description: >-
  Use this when building or restyling a personal library site from shelf photos,
  snippets, contradictions, or handed books.
---
# Personal library

Use this when someone wants a personal library site from their actual shelves: cataloging photos, snippets, contradictions, handed books, or restyling the library.

Build a static site the reader can host (default: Cloudflare Pages). Do not invent a GitHub repo or Vercel deploy unless they ask. Keep their existing catalog records when updating.

## Brief

White paper, `#111` ink, Avenir (fall back Helvetica), lowercase, lots of air, 1px rules. No cards, no shadows, no Inter, no purple gradients. Copy is lowercase, short, in the owner's voice. Use the impeccable design skill for any layout pass.

## Thinking structure (this is the product)

- **Shelves**, not Dewey as the front. Default hundreds: `000 tech`, `100 mind`, `200 spirit`, `300 world`, `400 money`, `600 work`, `700 making`, `800 writing`, `900 lives`. Novels sit with writing on 800. The owner can rename a shelf; keep the numbered hundreds.
- **Snippets are the unit.** A snippet is a line pulled from a book, or a photo of an underlined passage. Connections attach to snippets, not just books.
- **Contradictions first**, talks-to second. Disagreement is the interesting connection. A thin line between each contradiction pair. Related snippets nest under their parent with a thin left rule; each related snippet is its own row with its book title under it.
- **Handed** is "the books i always hand people to read." Mark `handed: true` when they name a book. A small black dot sits in front of the word handed (nav, filters, section header) and in front of any handed title. No stamp on the cover. The handed page explains the dot. Each numbered shelf lists handed books first.
- **Owner's note** is a boxed 1px `#111` section on the book page, titled `{name}'s note` in lowercase, above snippets.
- **Search** is a scrollable A–Z list by title (empty query shows the whole shelf).
- **Author pages:** clicking an author opens that author's shelf.
- **Buy** is a quiet Google search for author + title. No Amazon lock-in.

Default nav: catalog · search · snippets · contradictions · handed.

Default homepage line (they can rewrite): "these are the books on my actual shelves. just because i read them doesn't mean i agree with them. different perspectives help me connect dots i otherwise couldn't see."

Default contradictions intro: "whenever i read something i try to understand what the opposite view might be. this is my experiment to connect the contradictions in what i read."

Default handed intro: "the books i always hand people to read. the little black dot marks them."

Catalog heading: `on the shelf - N books` with the live count.

## Layout

Each shelf is one horizontal swipeable row. Titles sit under covers (not over them). Covers are large enough to read: about 180px tall on desktop, 165px on mobile, 240px on the book page.

## Cataloging from photos

When they send shelf photos, read spines. Do not invent titles, authors, or quotes. First-pass catalog is fine: title, author, a sensible shelf, a one-line blurb, a cover if you can find a real one (Open Library / ISBN). Status `shelf` for books they have. Look up ISBN/year from a real source. If a spine is cut off, ask rather than guess. Don't duplicate a title+author already in the catalog.

Handed only when they say so.

## Data

`books.json` records include: `id`, `title`, `author`, `isbn`, `isbn13`, `shelf`, `status`, `blurb`, `cover`, `year`, optional `handed`, optional `ownerNote`.

`snippets.json` records include: `id`, `bookId`, `text`, optional `photo`, `kind` (`text` or `photo`), `source` (e.g. `underline`), optional `talksTo` / `disagreesWith` (arrays of snippet ids), optional page.

Keep all existing records when adding. Don't fabricate snippet text.

## Site files (typical)

Pages: `index.html` (catalog), `search.html`, `book.html`, `author.html`, `snippet.html`, `snippets.html`, `contradictions.html`, `handed.html`. Shared `css/site.css` and `js/library.js`. Covers in `covers/{isbn}.jpg`.

## Hosting

Zip the site (exclude private pass notes and raw shelf-photo dumps). Deploy as a Production Direct Upload to an existing Cloudflare Pages project when they already have one. Do not create a new project or change domains unless they ask. After deploy, hard-reload and screenshot.

## After a visual change

Look at the real page. If related snippets are still a comma run, a truncated soup, or missing book context, fix it before calling it done.
